title: The deadline changed
prompt: Your supervisor moves a project deadline forward by three days. Finishing everything alone will require several late evenings.

choices.label: Ask to prioritize
choices.text: Explain the time limit and agree on the most important tasks.
choices.feedback: You made the limits visible. Some tasks were postponed, but the most important work moved forward.

choices.label: Work extra hours
choices.text: Keep the full scope and give up your evenings this week.
choices.feedback: You delivered more work, at the cost of recovery time. This may be difficult to sustain.

choices.label: Keep the original pace
choices.text: Finish what you can without discussing the new deadline.
choices.feedback: You protected your time, but your supervisor had no warning that the agreed work would be incomplete.

title: Learn a new tool
prompt: Your workplace is adopting unfamiliar software. A short optional course costs $450 and takes two weekends.

choices.label: Take the course
choices.text: Pay for structured practice outside work.
choices.feedback: You gained skills quickly, but paid in both money and free time.

choices.label: Use free practice resources
choices.text: Set aside small blocks of time for self-study.
choices.feedback: Your cash stayed available. Learning took longer and required a consistent routine.

choices.label: Wait for formal training
choices.text: Focus on current duties until the employer provides support.
choices.feedback: You avoided extra demands now, but the transition left you less prepared.

title: A mistake in the records
prompt: You notice a mistake in a report you already submitted. Correcting it will delay the team by an hour.

choices.label: Tell the team now
choices.text: Describe the error and help correct it.
choices.feedback: The delay was inconvenient. Catching the error before others relied on it protected trust.

choices.label: Double-check first
choices.text: Review your source material, then report what you confirm.
choices.feedback: You brought evidence with your concern, though the additional checking took time.

choices.label: Hope nobody notices
choices.feedback: The unresolved mistake stayed in the record. Avoiding an uncomfortable conversation created more uncertainty.

title: Lead the next project?
prompt: Your manager offers you a temporary team-lead assignment with a $600 bonus. It adds responsibility to your normal duties.

choices.label: Accept the full assignment
choices.text: Take the bonus and lead the team.
choices.feedback: You gained income and leadership practice. The added workload reduced your time outside work.

choices.label: Negotiate the workload
choices.text: Ask which existing tasks can be reassigned before accepting.
choices.feedback: A narrower assignment came with a smaller bonus and a more manageable workload.

choices.label: Decline this time
choices.feedback: You protected capacity. The bonus and this particular leadership opportunity went to someone else.

title: A teammate is falling behind
prompt: A teammate asks for help while you are finishing your own assignment. Both tasks are due tomorrow.

choices.label: Plan a short help session
choices.text: Offer thirty minutes and focus on the main obstacle.
choices.feedback: A clear time boundary let you support the team without taking over the task.

choices.label: Finish their work too
choices.text: Stay late and complete both assignments.
choices.feedback: The tasks were completed, but you absorbed the extra workload and your teammate missed practice.

choices.label: Focus on your assignment
choices.text: Suggest they ask the supervisor for help.
choices.feedback: You met your own commitment. The teammate still needed another source of support.

title: Feedback that stings
prompt: Your supervisor says your last presentation was hard to follow. You feel the effort you put in was overlooked.

choices.label: Ask for a specific example
choices.text: Find one improvement to practice before the next presentation.
choices.feedback: The feedback became a concrete next step instead of a judgment about your ability.

choices.label: Ask a peer to rehearse
choices.text: Use part of your free time to practice with someone you trust.
choices.feedback: Practice improved your preparation and cost some time outside normal duties.

choices.label: Dismiss the feedback
choices.text: Keep the same approach next time.
choices.feedback: You avoided the discomfort of changing, but the original communication problem remained.
